## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`--exclude` needs to take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because project policy requires that for every new flag under `cli/` so CI can set options through the environment. Apart from that policy gap, the filtering logic and its tests are consistent with the stated behavior.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect` uses it to skip files whose basename matches any of the patterns, and logs each skipped path. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end archive tests.

(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — The new `--exclude` flag uses a hard-coded `default=[]`, so setting `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` in the environment has no effect. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files without changing their command lines. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")` split on a documented separator such as `os.pathsep`, then update the `docs/flags.md:7` default column and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
